item.stem: The scale on a map indicates that 1 centimeter on the map represents 4 kilometers on the land. The distance between two towns on the map is 8 centimeters. How many kilometers apart are the two towns?

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
One centimeter on the map represents 8 kilometers on the land.

[Image: Map showing towns and a river]

About how far apart are Oxford and Smithville on the land?
reference_items.figure_description: A map enclosed in a rectangular border showing three towns indicated by black circular dots: Hatboro, Oxford, and Smithville. A thick curved line labeled 'Indian River' runs diagonally from the bottom-left edge up toward the top-right edge. Roads (thin lines) connect the towns across the map. Oxford is located in the upper-middle area, Hatboro is to the west, and Smithville is to the southeast. In the lower-right corner is a scale box displaying a line segment with vertical end ticks, labeled '1 cm = 8 km' below it.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
For this item, you have been given a cardboard ruler. If you do not have the cardboard ruler raise your hand. Use the map below and your ruler to answer this set of questions.

Marytown is a new town. The people of Marytown are planning their new town. They decided to put the town hall halfway between the lake and the forest, as shown on the map below. They made their measurements from the X's.

Marytown

[Image: Map of Marytown]

Add a park, a library, and a school to the map of Marytown using the following information.

C. The school should be halfway between the park and the library. On the map, mark with an X where you would put the school and write school below the X.

descriptors: School equidistant from park and library, X to X, measures to differ no more than 4mm
School is not equidistant (+/- 2 mm) from park and library
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: Park, library, and school need not to be in a straight line.
reference_items.figure_description:
A map of Marytown enclosed in an irregular rectangular border.
Near the top right inside the border, text states: "Scale: 1 cm represents 100 meters".
In the upper-left quadrant is a forest represented by a cluster of pine trees, with an "X" mark below it labeled "Forest".
Near the center of the map is an "X" mark labeled "Town Hall" below it.
In the lower-right quadrant is an outlined body of water with wavy horizontal lines inside, with an "X" mark directly above it labeled "Lake".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
